predecessors.name: Principality of Rostov-Suzdal (Vladimir-Suzdal)
predecessors.text: Rostov, 'the center of the Principality of Rostov' since the end of the 10th century, which Cliopatria draws inside its Rostov-Suzdal row (1056-1240)

successors.name: Grand Principality of Moscow
successors.text: Rostov, 'finally incorporated into the Grand Principality of Moscow in 1474'

ledger.x: 1219: Vasilko Konstantinovich takes Rostov as its own prince.
1389: the Rostov lands pass out of the grand principality's shape.
ledger.cpn: Principality of Vladimir-Suzdal (Grand Principality of Vladimir)

ledger.x: 1474: the Principality of Rostov ends in the Grand Principality of Moscow.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Rus'
wars.outcome: Prince Vasilko of Rostov was killed in the battle of the Sit River on 4 March 1238 ('died in the battle of the Sit River during the Mongol invasions'); the page records no change of land.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier of the principality; it is the town and a radius throughout.

sources.title: Vladimir-Suzdal (the article 'Principality of Rostov' redirects to)
